source.text: A reconstruction must permit discussion of a purported entity without silently settling the existence dispute.
source.locator: Retyped PDF pp. 1 and 3-5: McX, Pegasus, and descriptive paraphrase; these are not original journal page numbers

reading.speaker: W. V. Quine
reading.summary: A reconstruction must permit discussion of a purported entity without silently settling the existence dispute.

review.rationale: Imported design requirement; requires source-fidelity review. Mutation control: Moving McX's presupposition into Quine's accepted premises must be detected as an attribution error.

premises: Distinguish a quoted name, a purported referent, a mental representation and an existential commitment.
Track author versus opponent commitments and concessions for argument.
Make the denotation assumptions of the chosen formal language explicit.
Treat descriptive paraphrase as an explicit interpretation rather than silently introducing a denoting constant.
claim.conclusion: A model of one chosen regimentation is not by itself a resolution of all rival ontologies.
